title: NASA Launches Power to Explore Student Contest on Lunar Nuclear Power
content:
NASA’s Power to Explore Student Challenge officially launched on Tuesday, November 17, inviting kindergarten through 12th grade students across the United States to participate in a science, engineering, technology, and mathematics (STEM) competition. The challenge focuses on space nuclear power systems, asking students to learn about these technologies and illustrate how nuclear “batteries” could assist in powering their vision for lunar exploration. In addition to visual work, participants are required to write a short essay describing a personal “superpower” that would aid a mission. Submissions for the 2026-2027 cycle are due by March 1, 2027.

The initiative highlights the critical role of power sources in space missions, particularly in the harsh conditions of the Moon, which include freezing temperatures, long nights, and deep craters devoid of sunlight. Carl Sandifer, a program manager for NASA’s Space Reactors Division at the agency’s headquarters in Washington, stated that establishing a lunar base requires infrastructure to support human life and research. He noted that nuclear power could enable exploration in the permanently shadowed regions near the Moon’s South Pole, transport robust science payloads over long distances, and maintain instrument warmth during the lunar night. Sandifer added that the challenge prepares the next generation of explorers to design their own nuclear-powered Moon bases.

Entries for the contest consist of a 200-word essay and an original illustration. The essay must describe one unique power the student possesses that will help the mission, while the illustration must convey a vision of a nuclear-powered lunar base supporting both human and robotic exploration. The artwork should demonstrate an understanding of how radioisotope and fission-based power solutions enable exploration. Judges will evaluate the submissions in three distinct grade-level categories: K-4, 5-8, and 9-12.

One grand prize winner from each grade category will receive a trip for two to NASA’s Glenn Research Center in Cleveland, where they will learn about the personnel and technologies that enable NASA missions. Additionally, every student who submits an entry will receive a digital certificate and an invitation to a virtual event with NASA experts. This event is designed to teach participants about what energizes the NASA workforce to advance missions and sustain America’s leadership in space.

NASA and Future Engineers are currently seeking volunteers to judge the anticipated thousands of contest entries. U.S. residents older than 18 who are willing to commit approximately three hours of their time can register to judge through the Future Engineers website. The Power to Explore Student Challenge is funded by the NASA Science Mission Directorate and operates under the Radioisotope Power Systems Program within the Research and Technology Mission Directorate. Future Engineers administers the challenge through a contract with the NASA Center of Excellence for Collaborative Innovation.
summary: The thematics for the 2026-2027 Radioisotope Power Systems Power to Explore Student Challenge Credit: NASA / David Lam NASA’s Power to Explore Student Challenge kicked off Tuesday, Nov. 17.

title: StarSling Launches AI‑Powered CI Runners to Cut Costs and Speed Up Workflows
content:
StarSling, a Y Combinator P25 company founded by Yonas and Daniel, has launched a platform designed to provide self-improving continuous integration (CI) for repositories with high agent volume. The service offers fast GitHub Actions runners equipped with AI agents that generate pull requests to continuously optimize tests and workflows. Each CI job operates within its own ephemeral sandbox on Zen 5 machines and NVMe disks, featuring unlimited concurrency to allow bursts of agent pull requests to run simultaneously. Unlike other runners, StarSling’s infrastructure includes agents intended to reduce CI costs over time by generating optimizations through a dedicated CI harness.

The company highlights specific performance improvements achieved with its clients. Mastra, a user of the platform, now merges over 1,800 pull requests a month and saw its slowest workflow reduced from 29 minutes and 56 seconds on GitHub-hosted runners to 5 minutes and 06 seconds on StarSling, a 5.87x speedup. Additionally, StarSling agents identified an 11-month-old performance bottleneck in the better-auth project, resulting in a fix that made one of its test jobs 5.4x faster. The founders, who previously worked on StackShare and Netflix’s internal developer portal, developed StarSling after encountering CI bottlenecks while building AI agents for DevOps, where their own agents generated so many pull requests that job queues backed up for hours.

StarSling’s CI harness runs an agent loop that analyzes workflows, run logs, and machine telemetry to propose optimizations. The system tests the unchanged workflow side-by-side with the proposed change and uses a deterministic judgment to ensure the difference is statistically significant before shipping the winner as a pull request with benchmark evidence. The company reports that benchmarking open-source repositories on its runners yields an average 10x speedup in wall-clock time with 70% less runner time. Specific benchmarks include a 12.8x speedup for gogs, 5.5x for shellcheck, 3.9x for chatwoot, 11.7x for transfer.sh, and 36.4x for mirotalksfu.

To address infrastructure costs, the team initially built runners on AWS but found them too expensive. They subsequently convinced several sandbox providers to adopt Zen 5s and began publicly benchmarking them. StarSling now supports per-second billing and has released StarSling Disks, a feature providing persistent disks that offer a 4.9x speedup in dependency readiness compared to actions/cache. The company has also released skills for users who wish to perform these optimizations themselves using prompts, though StarSling argues that using their agents saves users from expending tokens and CI compute to find optimizations independently.

StarSling has converted CI optimization strategies from companies including OpenAI, Anthropic, and Linear into playbooks for agents. Users can access the platform via a provided documentation URL and receive 2,000 free minutes, with agents beginning to open pull requests once usage reaches approximately 10,000 minutes. The company has also announced a CI Challenge, offering a $1,000 reward if StarSling fails to save at least 10% on a user’s next CI bill. The launch post includes links to benchmarks, a demo of the disk feature, and the rules for the challenge, inviting feedback on the headless experience.
summary: We’re Yonas and Daniel and we’re building StarSling ( https://starsling. Dev ), fast GitHub Actions runners with AI agents that ship PRs to continuously improve your tests and workflows.

title: Nike’s new air sole technology can mix soft and firm cushioning
content:
Nike is introducing Tuned Air technology, which allows for the production of air-filled soles with varying levels of cushioning and stability. This new manufacturing process creates multiple air pockets within the sole, moving away from the previously uniform cushioning found in traditional Nike Air shoes. The approach mirrors the company’s 2024 launch of the Air Max 1000, which utilized 3D printing to achieve a uniform silhouette with distinct areas of support and flexibility.

This innovation builds on Nike’s nearly 50-year history of incorporating air pockets into footwear to enhance comfort and cushioning. By enabling a mix of soft and firm zones, the Tuned Air system offers a more tailored experience compared to older, consistent sole designs.
summary: In 2024, Nike announced its Air Max 1000, manufactured with a 3D‑printing process that creates a uniform silhouette while varying support and flexibility. Nike’s new Tuned Air technology produces multiple air pockets with differing cushioning levels, replacing the previous uniform cushioning across the sole of Nike Air shoes.

title: MacBook Neo gets $50 discount at Amazon, Best Buy, and Target ahead of Black Friday
content:
The MacBook Neo is currently available for $50 off at Amazon, Best Buy, and Target, a discount applicable to both storage configurations and all four color options. The 256GB model is priced at $649, while the 512GB version with Touch ID is reduced to $749. None of the retailers have specified an end date for the promotion, which represents the largest price drop since Apple increased the laptop’s MSRP by $100 in July due to the ongoing RAM crisis.

Apple’s budget-friendly laptop utilizes the A18 Pro processor, a chip originally designed for the iPhone 16 Pro, to maintain lower costs. Both the 256GB and 512GB models include 8GB of memory. While the device is not highly performant regarding storage speed and total memory, it is well-suited for everyday tasks, casual use, and students. A Verge colleague noted that the vivid 13-inch screen and speakers are superior to those found in many cheap and midrange Windows laptops.
summary: The MacBook Neo is discounted by $50 at several retailers, with the 256GB model priced at $649 and the 512GB model at $749. This is the largest price drop since Apple raised the laptop's MSRP by $100 in July due to the ongoing RAM crisis.

title: Nvidia board says it will not reinstate former CEO Jensen Huang
content:
Harvey Jones, the new chair of Nvidia’s board, stated during Tuesday’s quarterly earnings call that the board unanimously accepted the resignation of former CEO Jensen Huang and does not intend to reinstate him. Jones further announced that the company would not address questions regarding the circumstances of Huang’s resignation or any ongoing investigation during the call.

Earlier on Tuesday, Huang publicly expressed a desire to return. In a statement posted on X, he admitted that he did not live up to the company’s standards, expressed regret for his mistakes, and indicated that he would cooperate with the process.
summary: Nvidia's new board chair Harvey Jones confirmed that the board accepted former CEO Jensen Huang's resignation and will not reinstate him as CEO. Huang had earlier floated a return but said he did not meet company standards, regretted his mistakes, and would cooperate with investigations.

title: iFixit Finds Apple HomeView Hub Hard to Repair in Teardown
content:
iFixit’s teardown of Apple’s new HomeView hub reveals a device that is significantly more difficult to repair than recent iPads and HomePods. Despite the hub’s resemblance to a seven-inch tablet attached to a smart speaker, iFixit’s technicians encountered substantial challenges during disassembly. The process resulted in a ripped connector, a snapped speaker, and excessive force applied to the logic board, indicating that the device’s internal construction is far less repair-friendly than previously expected.

The tablet section of the HomeView presented the greatest difficulty due to specific design choices by Apple. While iFixit initially anticipated an easy disassembly similar to other recent Apple products, the actual teardown proved to be a demanding task for even skilled technicians.
summary: iFixit’s teardown of Apple’s HomeView hub revealed significant repair challenges, including a ripped connector, a snapped speaker, and damage to the logic board. The tablet section proved especially difficult to disassemble due to questionable design choices.

title: Jeff Bezos says he was heavily involved in picking new James Bond
content:
Amazon founder Jeff Bezos stated that he was “heavily involved” in casting Robert Pattinson as the new James Bond. Speaking at Semafor’s Silicon Valley and the World conference, Bezos described a rigorous selection process that began with a large group of candidates, which was narrowed down to five finalists. The team then conducted traditional screen tests for these five individuals before making the final decision on a Friday.

The announcement follows the recent confirmation of Pattinson’s role in the franchise, a move that aligns with his previous collaborations with director Denis Villeneuve, who is set to direct the next film for Amazon. Bezos emphasized the structured approach taken by the production team to finalize the choice for the iconic 007 character.
summary: Jeff Bezos stated at the Semafor conference that he was heavily involved in the final decision to cast Robert Pattinson as James Bond. Bezos described a tight process that involved down-selecting candidates to five finalists who then underwent screen tests.

title: ULA confirms Vulcan rocket failed early due to low booster performance
content:
United Launch Alliance (ULA) confirmed that its return-to-flight Vulcan rocket launch failed during the initial stages of the mission. The company stated that the vehicle experienced low booster performance just after liftoff, causing stage separation to occur at a low altitude and below the minimal velocity required to reach orbit. ULA reported that it lost telemetry and the mission approximately 10 minutes into the flight.

Additionally, ULA confirmed that the Centaur V upper stage and the solid rocket boosters performed nominally during the flight.
summary: ULA confirmed the Vulcan rocket failed approximately 10 minutes into flight. The failure was attributed to low booster performance causing stage separation at low altitude, while the Centaur V upper stage and solid rocket boosters performed nominally.

content:
Netflix has released the first teaser for the second season of 3 Body Problem, which is scheduled to premiere in January. The series, adapted from Liu Cixin’s award-winning novel, debuted in March 2024 and is part of a planned three-season run. The second season is described as the next installment in this limited series.

The show was created by David Benioff, D. B. Weiss, and Alexander Woo. The first season followed two primary timelines, one of which centered on Ye Wenjie, a young Chinese astrophysicist played by Rosalind Chao. She subsequently developed a method to send interstellar messages to potential extraterrestrial civilizations and received a response from a planet named Trisolaris. title: Hundreds of Optimizely sites deliver malware targeting crypto wallets and payment data
content:
Hundreds of sites that use the Optimizely website personalization platform were found to deliver a “potent malware cocktail” to visitors, according to researchers. The malware targeted cryptocurrency wallets, stole payment‑card data, cookies, and screenshots, and installed iOS exploit kits on iPhones and iPads.

ReportURI identified 178 affected sites, including CNN, Zoom, the BBC, and Salesforce. When the malware installed successfully, it swapped users’ cryptocurrency wallet addresses with attacker addresses. Other components of the payload skimmed payment‑card information, captured cookies and screenshots, and on iOS devices deployed the Coruna and DarkSword exploit kits.

The malicious code was inserted into JavaScript that Optimizely digitally signs and serves to customers. The script, which can be delivered directly from Optimizely or from a customer endpoint, runs on every page a customer serves. Attackers inserted their own code into a portion of each affected customer’s JavaScript and delivered it from cdn.optimizely.com, where a valid certificate for that domain signed the script.
summary: Hundreds of websites using the Optimizely website personalization platform served unsuspecting visitors a potent malware cocktail that targeted cryptocurrency wallets, stole payment card data, cookies, and screenshots, and delivered exploit kits for infecting iPhones and iPads, researchers said Tuesday. ReportURI said it identified 178 websites—including CNN, Zoom, the BBC, and Salesforce—that were affected.

title: ICEYE to buy Avio for $2.2B to create Europe’s first vertically integrated space company
content:
Finnish satellite developer ICEYE announced on Tuesday that it is pursuing the acquisition of Italian rocket‑maker Avio for more than $2.2 billion. The deal, intended to create Europe’s first fully vertically integrated end‑to‑end space company, is being offered as an all‑cash voluntary tender to Avio shareholders through an Italian subsidiary of ICEYE, which is led by the defense conglomerate Leonardo.  

Avio’s board of directors has acknowledged the notice from ICEYE and is reviewing the purchase proposal. The company is best known for building the Vega C rocket, a solid‑fuel launcher that can carry up to 3.3 metric tons (7,300 pounds) of payload to low‑Earth orbit. Since its first flight in 2022, the Vega C has successfully launched seven times out of eight attempts. It follows an earlier Vega model that achieved a 20‑for‑22 success record since its 2012 debut.
summary: Finnish satellite developer ICEYE announced a voluntary all‑cash tender offer to buy Italian rocket maker Avio for more than $2.2 billion. Avio, which builds the Vega C solid‑fuel launcher that has flown seven times in eight attempts since 2022, has said its board is considering the offer.

title: San Diego Ends Contracts with Flock and Ubicquia
content:
San Diego’s city council voted on Monday evening to terminate its contracts with two surveillance‑equipment vendors: Flock and Ubicquia. The decision marks the end of the city’s use of Flock’s cameras and Ubicquia’s smart streetlights.

San Diego is among the largest municipalities to end its relationship with Flock, a startup that has an estimated valuation of $8.3 billion. The move reflects the city’s shift away from the company’s surveillance technology.

Lily Irani of the Transparent and Responsible Use of Surveillance Technology (TRUST) SD Coalition said, “We fucking won!” She and her colleagues have been among the loudest critics of the vendors in recent years.
summary: San Diego city council voted to terminate contracts with surveillance equipment vendors Flock and Ubicquia. The city is one of the largest to end its relationship with Flock, a startup estimated to be worth $8.3 billion.

title: Microsoft launches Word, Excel, PowerPoint inside Copilot, calling it new OS for work
content: Opening the keynote at its Ignite event, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella outlined the company's vision for its new "frontier ecosystem," announcing Tuesday the general availability of Word, Excel, and PowerPoint inside Copilot, which he described as "the new OS for work." The announcement is a striking inversion of how we've traditionally used software. Rather than an app like Word being the attraction and Clippy the assistant to help you use it, Microsoft envisions the new Copilot integrations will see agents driving things, with the software packages riding shotgun. Applications will become plugin components of the agent's work, backed by an organizational knowledge layer that draws context from emails, meetings, calendars, chats, and files. Users will now be able to create documents, spreadsheets, and presentations directly in Copilot, with the resulting files remaining editable in their respective Office applications. summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella announced at the Ignite keynote that Word, Excel and PowerPoint are now generally available inside Copilot, which he described as "the new OS for work." content:
England’s qualifications regulator, Ofqual, has warned that students caught using AI or smart glasses to cheat could face “life-altering” penalties. Head of Ofqual Ian Bauckham stated that such actions could lead to disqualification from GCSEs, A-levels, and other qualifications. The regulator specifically noted that using AI in assessed coursework is a serious offense.

In addition to student sanctions, Bauckham called for retailers to be barred from marketing wearable technology for the purpose of exam cheating. This stance highlights the regulator’s focus on preventing the use of technological aids during assessments.
summary: England’s qualifications regulator Ofqual warned that students caught using AI or smart glasses could be disqualified from GCSEs, A-levels and other qualifications. Ofqual head Ian Bauckham called the penalties “life‑altering” and urged retailers to stop marketing wearable technology for exam cheating.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Ukraine drones hit Kerch Bridge for second night, bridge closed
content: Ukraine struck the Kerch Bridge linking Russia to annexed Crimea for a second consecutive night, forcing its closure. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called the operation unprecedented and said it had been prepared over several weeks.
summary: Ukraine struck the Kerch Bridge linking Russia to annexed Crimea for a second consecutive night, forcing its closure. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy described the operation as unprecedented and said it had been prepared over several weeks.

title: Anti-regime protest erupts in western Iranian city after deadly bus crash
content: A protest sparked by a deadly bus crash in a western Iranian city turned into a new anti-regime protest with hundreds chanting "Death to the dictator."
summary: A protest in a western Iranian city was sparked by a deadly bus crash. The demonstration turned into an anti‑regime rally with hundreds chanting “Death to the dictator.”

title: US attacks Qeshm Island after mines set fire to at least five ships in Strait of Hormuz
content: Iran reports that the U.S. military conducted several attacks on Qeshm Island in southern Iran. The strikes followed earlier incidents in which mines in the Strait of Hormuz set fire to at least five ships.
summary: Iran says the US military carried out several attacks on Qeshm Island in southern Iran. Earlier in the day, mines in the Strait of Hormuz set fire to at least five ships.

title: Melbourne Cup horse So You Are euthanised then dumped at Sydney landfill
content: REC Equine Specialists confirmed that the Melbourne Cup racehorse So You Are was euthanised, then collected by a contracted provider and taken to a licensed landfill. The horse was later discovered at a Sydney waste facility. The practice apologized, stating the animal should have been promptly and respectfully buried.
summary: REC Equine Specialists said So You Are was euthanised, collected by a contracted provider and taken to a licensed landfill. The practice apologised, saying the horse should have been promptly and respectfully buried.
author: Euronews

title: Pope Leo XIV's South American tour includes flying rosary bracelet, Andes helicopter ride
content: Pope Leo XIV’s South American tour produced several viral moments, including an unexpected encounter with a flying rosary bracelet and a helicopter journey that took him into Peru’s remote Andes. These incidents were highlighted as memorable highlights of the trip.
summary: Pope Leo XIV's South American tour featured several memorable moments. The tour included an unexpected encounter with a flying rosary bracelet and a helicopter journey into Peru's remote Andes.

title: German defence minister slams US warning on Ukraine deep strikes, UK minister backs them
content: German Defence Minister Boris Pistorius called the US' warning "quite a stupid thing," while his British counterpart Wes Streeting said there was "no doubt" in his mind that Ukraine's long-range strikes had "helped to degrade Putin's war machine."
summary: German defence minister slams US warning on Ukraine deep strikes, UK minister backs them.

title: Jensen Huang says he’d be honoured to return as Nvidia CEO
content: Jensen Huang, in his first public comment since resigning from Nvidia, said he would be honoured to return to his job as CEO, noting support from the tech world. The remark comes ahead of Nvidia’s earnings call on Tuesday, where analysts anticipate a 90 % revenue increase to roughly $109 billion.
summary: Jensen Huang made his first public statement since resigning from Nvidia, saying he would be honoured to return to his job. The comment came ahead of the group’s earnings call on Tuesday, where analysts expect a 90% revenue jump to about $109 billion.

title: Netanyahu faces setbacks as Knesset prepares to elect speaker opposed to him
content: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s party, which suffered heavy losses in Israel’s Oct. 27 election, has repeatedly asserted that the vote was “stolen” by Arab‑led parties, possibly with foreign assistance. According to FRANCE 24’s Noga Tarnopolsky in Jerusalem, those claims are now appearing to crumble as the Israeli parliament prepares to choose a new Knesset speaker who opposes Netanyahu. The upcoming speaker vote represents a further setback for the prime minister as he seeks to retain power.
summary: Since heavy losses in Israel’s Oct. 27 election, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s party has repeatedly claimed the vote was “stolen” by Arab‑led parties, possibly with foreign assistance. Those claims appear to be crumbling as the Israeli parliament prepares to select a new Knesset speaker who opposes him.
author: France 24

title: AI-generated fake voting profiles threaten Nigeria's January election
content:
Concerns have surfaced that artificial intelligence has been employed to create fake voting profiles in the lead‑up to Nigeria’s high‑stakes general election scheduled for January. The reports highlight the potential for AI‑generated misinformation to influence voter perceptions during the campaign period.

Separately, Nigeria’s mining marshal has reportedly gone underground to investigate the individuals and organizations involved in the country’s extensive illegal mining industry. The initiative aims to uncover the networks that sustain these illicit operations.

In a different region, archaeologists in northern Sudan have announced a discovery that may represent the ancient site of the largest church ever built in medieval Nubia. The find could shed light on one of the area’s most significant Christian sites from the medieval period.
summary: AI has been used to generate fake voting profiles ahead of Nigeria's high-stakes general election in January. Meanwhile, Nigeria's mining marshal is investigating illegal mining, and a discovery in northern Sudan may be the site of the largest church in medieval Nubia.
author: France 24

title: Israeli Parliament Elects Matan Kahana, Eisenkot Ally, as New Speaker
content: The Israeli parliament elected former special‑forces soldier Matan Kahana as speaker on Tuesday. Kahana is identified as an ally of Gadi Eisenkot, the party leader who is working to form the next government and replace Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. He is expected to begin, as early as Wednesday, reversing much of Netanyahu’s agenda.
summary: The Israeli parliament elected Matan Kahana, an ally of Gadi Eisenkot, as speaker. Kahana, a former special forces soldier, is expected as soon as Wednesday to start undoing much of Netanyahu's agenda.
author: France 24

title: US, Mexico and Bolivia lose measles‑free status as deaths mount
content:
International health officials announced Tuesday that the United States has lost its measles-free status, a designation it shares with Mexico and Bolivia, which have also lost their measles-elimination status. The announcement comes as the highly contagious virus spreads at its fastest rate in over three decades.

Measles has been spreading throughout the Americas since 2024, a trend attributed to declining vaccination rates for various diseases in the United States and globally.
summary: US, Mexico and Bolivia lose measles‑free status as deaths mount.
author: France 24

title: WHO warns antimicrobial resistance threatens modern medicine
content:
The World Health Organization has warned that antimicrobial resistance (AMR) poses a growing threat to modern medicine. Senior WHO officials said that although countries have increased their efforts to tackle AMR, the pace of progress in prevention, diagnosis and the appropriate use of antibiotics is still too slow to reach global targets.

In a Monday briefing, WHO’s Acting Director of the AMR Department, Jean Pierre Nyemazi, was interviewed by France 24’s Sharon Gaffney. The officials highlighted the need for faster action to curb the spread of drug‑resistant bacteria and protect the effectiveness of antibiotics worldwide.
summary: Senior World Health Organization officials said on Monday that the spread of antimicrobial resistance is threatening modern medicine despite progress against drug‑resistant bacteria. They added that although countries have expanded efforts, progress in prevention, diagnosis and appropriate antibiotic use remains too slow to meet global targets.
author: France 24

title: Nvidia board says co‑founder Jensen Huang will not return as CEO
content: On Tuesday, Nvidia’s board chairman ruled out bringing co‑founder Jensen Huang back as CEO. The chipmaker, which forecast stronger‑than‑expected quarterly sales, is now facing growing questions over its leadership, national‑security exposure and long‑term strategy following Huang’s abrupt departure.
summary: Nvidia's board chairman said on Tuesday that co‑founder Jensen Huang will not be brought back as CEO. title: Guinea court jails 22 officials and 200 illegal miners in Siguiri crackdown
content: A court in Conakry has sentenced 22 former local officials from the gold‑rich northeastern Siguiri region to prison, along with 200 individuals charged with illegal mining. The action is part of a broader crackdown that has caused thousands of miners to flee into Mali.
summary: A Conakry court jailed 22 former local officials from the gold‑rich Siguiri region and 200 people accused of illegal mining. The crackdown forced thousands to flee into Mali.

content:
Former President Hashim Thaci received a second conviction in The Hague, being found guilty of attempting to influence witnesses in his war‑crimes trial.  

The ruling has sparked renewed debate in Kosovo over the Kosovo Specialist Chambers, the court that issued the conviction, and broader questions of justice in the country.

content: Humanitarian workers on Ukraine’s frontline must balance staying close to the communities they serve with the increased dangers of operating in a conflict zone, said the top UN official in Ukraine. The statement highlights the challenge of providing aid amid ongoing hostilities.
summary: Humanitarian workers providing support to communities on the frontline of the war between Ukraine and Russia must balance staying close to those in need with heightened risks. The top UN official in Ukraine made this assessment.

content: At his final ASEAN Summit in Manila, UN Secretary‑General António Guterres addressed regional leaders on Monday. He urged stronger collaboration with the Association of Southeast Asian Nations and called for an end to the crisis in Myanmar.

content: COP31 has entered a decisive week, with climate talks confronting a political test. title: Hugh Jackman, Rebel Wilson and 150 Australian artists join call to block Woodside gas development near Scott Reef

content:
An eight‑year‑old Haitian boy was detained by immigration agents in San Diego on 4 November. He was placed in restraints and subsequently transferred to a facility in Texas. The boy was separated from his family during this federal custody period.

According to the NGO Survival International, members of the Awá people, who live in voluntary isolation, arrived on Monday in a village and made contact with a government team in a “historic encounter”.

content:
St Kitts and Nevis will wind down its citizenship‑by‑investment programme after the European Union warned it could revoke the country’s visa‑free access. The announcement was made on Friday by Terrance Drew, the prime minister of the twin‑island Caribbean nation.

The premier of Nevis said ending the lucrative scheme threatens the economy and the nation’s ability to support people in need. Caribbean nations have voiced fear that shutting the programme could have broader economic repercussions.
summary: Prime Minister Terrance Drew announced on Friday that St Kitts and Nevis will wind down its citizenship‑by‑investment programme. He said the EU’s warning that visa‑free access could be ended threatens the country’s economy and its ability to support people in need.

title: Jessica Watkins 3D prints human cells and tissues aboard ISS
content:
NASA astronaut Jessica Watkins, the commander of Crew-13, has been conducting an experiment aboard the International Space Station (ISS) that involves 3D-printing human cells and tissues. The research, known as InSPA-Auxilium Bioprinter-Cell Printing, takes place inside the station’s Life Sciences Glovebox, a contained research environment described by Watkins as one of her favorite places to work. In a photograph shared on social media and captured by crewmate Anil Menon, Watkins is seen with her hands and arms inside the sealed glovebox, mixing samples of living cells with a bioink. This mixture is then inserted into a specialized cartridge for the printing process.

The experiment leverages the microgravity environment of the ISS to manufacture human liver, kidney, and cartilage tissue. Watkins noted that this work is part of a broader effort to use the orbital laboratory to reshape understanding in biology, medicine, and engineering, ultimately aiming to improve life on Earth. Specifically, the current phase of the experiment is designed to explore the 3D printing of human cartilage tissue in microgravity, with the long-term goal of supporting future human patients both in space and on Earth.

The unique conditions of the ISS allow for biological experiments that are not possible on the planet’s surface. Although gravity is still present on the station, objects and people remain in a state of constant freefall, resulting in total weightlessness that mimics the complete absence of gravity. This environment enables researchers to test and explore biological processes beyond the gravitational confines of Earth, making the station an ideal location for such specialized research.
summary: NASA astronaut Jessica Watkins works in the Life Sciences Glovebox on the ISS. (Image credit: Jessica Watkins/NASA) Astronauts get tasked with all kinds of weird science aboard the International Space Station.
author: Space.com

title: NASA Invites Public to Flash VGR in Morse Code for Voyager 1 Light-Day Milestone
content:
NASA is inviting people worldwide to participate in a public event called "Shine Bright for Voyager's Light-Day" to honor its Voyager 1 spacecraft as it approaches a historic distance from Earth. The celebration is scheduled for after sunset on Tuesday, Nov. 17, the day before Voyager 1 becomes one light-day away from Earth. This milestone represents the distance light travels in a single day, which is approximately 16 billion miles (26 billion kilometers). The event serves as a symbolic tribute to the spacecraft, which was launched on Sept. 5, 1977, and is currently the most distant human-made object from Earth.

Participants are encouraged to create a symbolic wave of golden light around the planet by flashing the spacecraft’s three-letter mission call sign, VGR, in Morse code. The agency suggests using a flashlight, phone, bike light, or other portable light source to send the signal skyward. For those unfamiliar with Morse code, NASA has developed an automated flasher accessible via smartphone or tablet browsers. The specific sequence consists of three quick flashes and one long flash for V, two long flashes and one quick flash for G, and one quick flash, one long flash, and another quick flash for R. NASA officials recommend repeating this sequence for about a minute.

The agency clarifies that the light signals are not an attempt to communicate with Voyager 1, as the spacecraft is too far away for such signals to reach it. Even radio signals traveling at the speed of light take approximately 24 hours to reach the probe, and NASA maintains contact using its Deep Space Network of radio dishes. Instead, the goal is to create a worldwide display of light marking a milestone nearly five decades in the making. Participants are also invited to photograph or record their light signals and share them on social media by tagging NASA’s official account, @NASA.

Following the public celebration, NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California will host a moderated discussion on Thursday, Nov. 19, at 12 p.m. EST (1700 GMT). The session will feature Voyager mission team members and NASA leadership discussing the current status of both Voyager spacecraft, their unique scientific observations in interstellar space, and the engineering challenges of keeping the nearly 50-year-old probes operational. A question-and-answer session with media and audience members will follow the discussion.

NASA will also provide a preview of an upcoming Voyager documentary planned for release in 2027, coinciding with the mission's 50th anniversary. While Voyager 1 is set to reach the one-light-day milestone on Nov. 18, 2026, its twin, Voyager 2, is expected to reach the same distance in November 2035. The two spacecraft took different routes through the solar system. Additional details regarding the automated VGR flasher and step-by-step Morse code instructions are available online.
summary: As NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft prepares to reach a historic distance from Earth, the agency is inviting people around the world to celebrate by shining a light into the night sky in honor of humanity's farthest-flung spacecraft. The event, called "Shine Bright for Voyager's Light-Day," will take place after sunset on Tuesday (Nov.

title: NASA Surveyor 6 Makes First Powered Liftoff From Lunar Surface
content:
NASA’s Surveyor 6 marked a historic milestone on November 17, 1967, when it became the first spacecraft to lift off from the lunar surface. The probe, which had been launched to the Moon on November 7 and had softly landed in the Sinus Medii on November 10, fired its engines for 2.5 seconds during an engineering test. The brief thrust raised the lander 12 feet (about 3.7 meters) into the air and moved it roughly 8 feet (2 meters) west of its original touchdown point, the first powered liftoff from another celestial body.

During the hop, Surveyor 6’s cameras captured images of the landing site and the surface disturbances caused by the initial touchdown and by the rocket exhaust. Flight controllers on Earth could see the landing‑pad prints and the imprint left by the engines, confirming that the lander’s rockets could be restarted and operated on the Moon. The maneuver also provided scientists with valuable data for a soil‑mechanics investigation, as the photographs taken after the hop offered insight into how lunar regolith responded to the landing and to the brief launch.

Surveyor 6 carried a bar magnet on its footpad, allowing researchers to test the magnetic properties of the lunar soil at the landing site. Over its 16‑day stay on the Moon, the probe took nearly 30,000 photographs before shutting down on November 26 when the lunar night began. As the sixth and penultimate mission of NASA’s Surveyor program, its successful hop demonstrated a capability that would later prove essential for the Apollo astronauts, who needed a way to return home after visiting the Moon.

NASA’s mission overview noted that the hop “proved that a spacecraft could land on the Moon, and then lift off and take flight once more.” The Lunar and Planetary Institute added that the maneuver “contributed to the soil mechanics investigation” and helped scientists study the effects of firing rocket engines close to the lunar surface. For more on this event and other milestones in space history, the On This Day In Space archive and accompanying videos are available on YouTube.
summary: On November 17, 1967, NASA's Surveyor 6 spacecraft executed the first powered liftoff from another celestial body by firing its engines for 2.5 seconds. This engineering test moved the probe 8 feet from its original landing site and proved that spacecraft could land and then lift off from the moon.
author: Space.com

title: New Edward Hopper biography reveals wife's fury over erased credit and sexual themes
content: He is the maestro of American melancholy. But in a new biography, the artist is called a ‘sadist’ and a ‘prize hog’ by his wife – who was aghast to see their domestic and bedroom problems surface in his most famous works It should have been a happy occasion. In 1950, an Edward Hopper retrospective was staged at the Whitney Museum of American Art in New York – but the artist’s wife, the painter Josephine (Jo) Nivison Hopper, was in a fury. The show’s catalogue, written by the museum’s director, had originally stated that in 1924 Edward “married the artist Josephine Nivison Hopper”, yet in the final version, the phrase “the artist” had been removed. “I’m not allowed to exist even in my husband’s biography,” Jo seethed in a private notebook that has just come to light. “And that’s all right with EH.” Due to her own strenuous efforts, Jo not only exists, but is a vital protagonist in my new biography of Edward Hopper. Jo once contemplated writing her husband’s biography herself, having amassed such an overwhelming body of material documenting their tumultuous marriage. As Edward’s creative partner, muse, curator, producer and unofficial manager, Jo produced 35 years’ worth of daily diaries, almost 100 notebooks, reels of letters, and four ledger books documenting Edward’s works.
summary: He is the maestro of American melancholy. But in a new biography, the artist is called a ‘sadist’ and a ‘prize hog’ by his wife – who was aghast to see their domestic and bedroom problems surface in his most famous works It should have been a happy occasion.
author: Guardian Culture

title: I Play Rocky Marks 50th Anniversary of Sylvester Stallone's Boxing Film
content:
Sylvester Stallone’s Oscar‑winning drama “Rocky” turns 50 this year, and the new film I Play Rocky is helping to keep the boxing hero’s myth alive. The new movie draws on the original story’s parallels: an unknown writer with an improbable dream, a skeptical film industry, and a refusal to accept the odds.

Stallone’s own struggle to break into Hollywood and bring his breakthrough script to the screen mirrors the underdog narrative he created. The original film, produced on a $1 million budget, became the highest‑grossing movie of 1976 and won the Academy Award for Best Picture against a highly competitive field.

Its enduring appeal is evident in the continued expansion of the franchise—six Rocky films, three Creed sequels, a Broadway musical, and numerous documentaries, novelizations, and video games. Even critics who once dismissed the film, such as the New York Times and Gene Siskel, were unable to stop its lasting cultural impact.

The screenplay, written in just three and a half days and never initially conceived as intellectual property, has evolved into a contemporary folklore that continues to inspire new adaptations.
summary: Peter Farrelly's documentary I Play Rocky explores the parallels between Sylvester Stallone's real-life career struggles and his 1976 film Rocky. The article notes that the original movie has evolved into a cultural legend, spawning six sequels, three Creed films, and other media.
author: Guardian Culture

title: ‘Sorry, I’m still in love with Daniel Craig’: Ralph Fiennes, Brad Pitt and more react to Robert Pattinson as James Bond
content:
Former 007 George Lazenby has publicly expressed support for the decision to cast Robert Pattinson as the next James Bond. The news has prompted a range of reactions from film‑industry figures, including Ralph Fiennes and Brad Pitt, though the article only details Pitt’s comments. While promoting his new film, The Further Mis‑Adventures of Cliff Booth, Pitt was asked about Pattinson and said, “I think it’s a great choice. I love what that guy’s been doing. He’s been making such interesting choices, and then for him to balance it out, it’s really cool.” He followed up with a playful pitch for a villain role in Bond 26, winking at the camera and saying, “Get Denis Villeneuve on the flip phone. Let’s go.”

The piece also notes that director Robert Eggers revealed what Pattinson was doing when the casting announcement broke. Other topics covered include Peter Bradshaw’s take, Pattinson’s journey to the role, and a look at Bond’s bankability. The article presents these reactions and insights without adding further context or speculation.
summary: Former 007 George Lazenby was supportive while The Lighthouse director Robert Eggers reveals what Pattinson was doing when the news broke • Robert Pattinson is James Bond. What happens next?
author: Guardian Culture

title: Call my (estate) agent! Why celebrities are always buying each other’s homes
content:
Celebrities continue to trade high‑profile homes among themselves, according to recent reports. Last year, actor Austin Butler purchased a mansion from Brad Pitt. A month earlier, Pitt had acquired a different mansion from a member of the band The Killers.

In 2022, singer Adele bought Sylvester Stallone’s former residence, but only if Stallone allowed her to keep his Rocky statue. More recently, actor Aaron Paul sold a house he had bought from Jim Parsons. Parsons had previously bought the property from Robert Pattinson, and the house had earlier belonged to Noah Wyle, Kareem Abdul‑Jabbar, Tim Curry and the director of Legally Blonde.

These transactions illustrate how celebrity real‑estate ownership often circulates within a tight circle of high‑profile buyers.
summary: If you’re seeking a discreet mansion with secluded grounds and plenty of room for your own memorabilia, you may want to remember Joe Pesci’s mistakes before trying the open market Last year, Austin Butler bought a mansion from Brad Pitt. The month before, Brad Pitt bought a mansion from one of the Killers.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Documentary 'The Last Critic' Spotlights Robert Christgau, Dean of American Rock Critics
content: Beloved for his savage takedowns and rhapsodic raves, the legendary Village Voice reviewer opens up in a candid new documentary Rows and rows of CDs, albums, cassettes and books creak and groan on shelves that snake around the walls and choke the halls of an apartment in New York City’s East Village. The clutter that sprawls through its rooms is so dense it suggests the twistiest parts of a Moroccan medina or a warren no self-respecting rabbit would allow. Buried amid the muddle is a man hunched over a computer keyboard, clacking out words meant to make sense of all the sounds that this physical media holds. Welcome to the lair of Robert Christgau, the self-declared “Dean of American Rock Critics”, as seen in a new documentary provocatively titled The Last Critic. “Bob is someone who has probably listened to more music, and published more words about music, than anyone to walk the face of the earth, and he’s still doing it in his mid-80s,” says Matty Wishnow, who directed the film. “It’s a career that’s both unprecedented and unrepeatable.”
summary: The new documentary 'The Last Critic' follows Robert Christgau, the self-declared Dean of American Rock Critics, as he reviews music in his cluttered East Village apartment. Director Matty Wishnow highlights Christgau's prolific career, noting he has listened to and written about more music than anyone else, even in his mid‑80s.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Eight‑hour PBS docuseries explores crime and punishment history in America
content: An eight-hour docuseries looks back to explore the many problems and injustices that have helped to further break a broken system Lynn Novick’s new film for PBS is an epic, an eight-hour examination of Crime & Punishment in America. Beginning with justice in tribal societies, the documentary follows the arc of US history and ends in today’s troubled prison system, with the story of a podcast produced by prisoners in San Quentin and scenes from Rikers Island. “I’ve been working with Ken Burns on films about American history for all of my career, basically, and looked at the story of America through many different perspectives,” Novick said. “And honestly, I had never paid that much attention to the question of the justice system until 14 years ago, I had the opportunity to teach, to do a guest lecture in a college class inside a prison.”
summary: Eight‑hour PBS docuseries explores crime and punishment history in America.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Jon Stewart calls Trump administration's response to FAA ground stop chaotic
content: Late-night hosts discussed the administration’s unhelpful response to the FAA’s rare ground stop this weekend Late-night hosts responded to the FAA’s sudden, rare ground stop as Donald Trump shirks any responsibility for the transportation crisis.
summary: Jon Stewart calls Trump administration's response to FAA ground stop chaotic.

title: Mia Latter says prison message from Russell Brand is 'upsetting'
content: Mia Latter spoke to the BBC after the jailed comedian claimed he was innocent of offences against four other women, in comments on a podcast following his convction.
summary: Mia Latter spoke to the BBC about a prison message from Russell Brand. Brand said he was innocent of offences against four other women in comments on a podcast following his convction.
author: BBC Entertainment

title: Max Dowman scores winner for England U21s, breaks another record
content:
Max Dowman scored the winning goal in England’s 3-2 under-21 victory over France, a performance that added to a list of recent records. The midfielder’s winner eclipsed a previous mark set by Jude Bellingham. The match took place in poor conditions at Ashton Gate, where Dowman provided the final say in the contest.

The article highlights a series of achievements for the teenager, including becoming the youngest goalscorer in the UEFA Youth League while playing for Arsenal Under-19s at age 14. He also became the youngest player to feature in the Champions League at age 15 and 308 days. More recently, Dowman became the Premier League’s youngest goalscorer and the youngest player to earn a Premier League winner’s medal. Last month, he was presented with three Guinness World Records.
summary: Max Dowman scored the winning goal in England's 3-2 victory over France in the under‑21s match at Ashton Gate. The goal also saw him break another record, becoming the youngest player to earn a Premier League winner’s medal and adding a third Guinness World Record.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Wiegman extends England contract to 2029, citing young talent
content:
Sarina Wiegman has extended her contract as England head coach until the end of the 2029 European Championship, citing the high potential of emerging young players as a key factor in her decision. Her previous agreement was set to expire next year. The Lionesses manager named her squad on Tuesday for the two-leg World Cup qualifying playoff against Ukraine in December.

This announcement included the first senior call-ups for striker Isobel Goodwin and goalkeeper Katie Cox. Wiegman expressed excitement regarding the potential within the squad, highlighting these new additions as central to the team’s future direction.
summary: Sarina Wiegman extended her contract as England head coach until the end of the 2029 European Championship, citing the high potential of emerging players. She named a squad for the World Cup qualifying playoff against Ukraine, including first senior call-ups for striker Isobel Goodwin and goalkeeper Katie Cox.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Bryson DeChambeau joins DP World Tour after LIV Golf bankruptcy
content:
Bryson DeChambeau, a player in ‘category one’ status after his US Open win, is currently ineligible for the PGA Tour because of a blanket ban. The two‑time major champion has now confirmed that he will join the DP World Tour for the next season, following the demise of LIV Golf.  

DeChambeau heads a roster of high‑profile names who are set to compete regularly in Europe in 2027 after LIV’s bankruptcy. The golfer’s future had been shrouded in intrigue; as a poster boy for LIV and its Saudi‑Arabian‑backed disruption scheme, he appeared reluctant to return to traditional tours.  

The PGA Tour has not offered an easy pathway for him, although his performances in Europe could theoretically allow a return. Cards will become available on the PGA Tour for 2028 through DP World Tour rankings. DeChambeau’s growing focus on content creation has fueled speculation that he might skip mainstream competition entirely.
summary: Bryson DeChambeau has confirmed his move to the DP World Tour for the 2027 season following the bankruptcy of LIV Golf. The two-time major winner is currently ineligible for the PGA Tour due to a blanket ban but can earn a card for 2028 through DP World Tour rankings.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Pocognoli’s ambition for Scotland’s play style faces risk of being unworkable
content:
The Scottish national team suffered a 4‑0 defeat to a second‑string Switzerland, a result that has intensified tactical concerns about head coach Sébastien Pocognoli’s suitability. This loss comes just six games into his tenure, prompting the Scottish Football Association to look to past experiences for guidance during a challenging international window.

Steve Clarke’s early days in charge were similarly fraught, with successive 4‑0 defeats by Belgium and Russia in 2019 leaving him questioning whether he should have remained in club management. A later revival saw Clarke lead Scotland to three of four major tournaments, a record that highlighted his pragmatic approach and decades of coaching experience.

Pocognoli, however, is described as moving toward a “dreamy ideologue” model, with aspirations for how Scotland must play deemed potentially unworkable. The meek nature of the team’s collapse in the Switzerland match and the Belgian assessment—laden with overpraise—have raised eyebrows among observers.
summary: The 4-0 loss to Switzerland has raised tactical concerns about the head coach’s suitability, just six games into the job. Pocognoli, who has only been in charge for six games, is at risk of being seen as a dreamy ideologue whose aspiration for how Scotland must play is unworkable.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Wayne Rooney Reveals He Contemplated Suicide During Manchester United Career
content:
Former England striker Wayne Rooney has revealed that during his time at Manchester United he once contemplated taking his own life. In a recent appearance on the Life At The Midpoint with Gabby Logan podcast, Rooney described a period when his mental health deteriorated despite his success on the pitch.

Rooney said that, even while thriving as a player, he was struggling off the field. He was newly married and a father to his eldest child, Kai, yet he would spend two days at a time drinking at home. At his lowest point, he considered suicide, a thought he later described as selfish.

He explained that he hid away because he did not want Kai to see him in that state, reflecting on how he struggled to cope with the pressure and his personal challenges.
summary: Former England striker Wayne Rooney said he had a period during his Manchester United career when he contemplated suicide. He described drinking for two days at a time and hiding away to avoid his eldest son Kai seeing him in distress.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Arsenal legend Peter Storey dies aged 81
content:
Arsenal has paid tribute to Peter Storey, the former England midfielder and key member of the 1971 Double-winning team, who has died at the age of 81. Storey made 501 appearances for the club from 1965, a record that places him eighth on their all-time appearances list. He was part of the Bertie Mee side that secured both the First Division title and the FA Cup during a season described as one of the most celebrated in Arsenal’s history.

The former international also earned 19 caps for England. Storey concluded his professional career at Fulham.
summary: Peter Storey, who made 501 appearances for Arsenal and won 19 England caps, died at age 81. He was a key member of the 1971 Double-winning team under Bertie Mee.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Philippe Diallo launches campaign to challenge Gianni Infantino for FIFA presidency
content:
Philippe Diallo, the French Football Federation president, officially launched his campaign for the FIFA presidency in Paris on Tuesday, announcing his intention to challenge Gianni Infantino. He said he had received strong signs of support from other continents.

Diallo also stated that he had contacted Kozo Tashima, who announced his candidacy earlier this month, and would try to convince him to join forces. He did not specify whether he would ask Tashima to stand aside, noting that their approaches share the same assessments and values.
summary: Philippe Diallo launches campaign to challenge Gianni Infantino for FIFA presidency.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Rassie Erasmus banned for six matches over match‑fixing remarks
content:
Rugby officials have imposed a six‑match ban on Springboks head coach Rassie Erasmus, effective immediately. The sanction follows a Monday tirade in which Erasmus questioned whether match officials were involved in match‑fixing during the Nations Championship finals held at Twickenham.

Erasmus also criticized the standard of refereeing in the tournament, alleging a bias in favour of northern‑hemisphere teams. World Rugby’s disciplinary panel reviewed the incident and concluded that the threshold for serious misconduct had been met. The ban will prevent Erasmus from coaching any international match for the next six games.
summary: Rassie Erasmus has been banned for six international matches by World Rugby. The ban follows his Monday rant questioning match‑fixing and criticizing refereeing in the Nations Championship.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Jacob Bethell to miss England’s South Africa Test tour after knee surgery
content: Jacob Bethell will miss England’s Test tour of South Africa because he requires additional surgery on the knee injury that has sidelined him since July.
summary: Jacob Bethell will miss England’s Test tour of South Africa because he requires more surgery on the knee injury. The injury has kept him out since July.

title: Former Arsenal midfielder Peter Storey, 1970-71 Double winner, dies at 81
content: Former Arsenal and England midfielder Peter Storey, who contributed to the Gunners’ 1970‑71 Double triumph, has died at the age of 81. The announcement confirms his passing but provides no further details.
summary: Peter Storey, a former Arsenal and England midfielder, died at the age of 81. He helped Arsenal win the Double in the 1970-71 season.

content: Wayne Rooney has revealed that he considered taking his own life during his time at Manchester United. The former player stated that he was speaking with a therapist at the time to help determine the cause of his struggles.

title: Democratic lawmakers target Trump administration over U.S. losing measles elimination status
content: Democratic lawmakers are criticizing the Trump administration following the U.S. loss of its measles elimination status. The country officially lost this designation on Tuesday, the first time since earning it over two-and-a-half decades ago. In the last two years, the U.S. has recorded over 7,700 cases of measles.
summary: Democratic lawmakers are going after the Trump administration over the U. S.

title: PETA urges Trump to end annual turkey pardon ceremony
content: People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals (PETA) sent a letter to President Trump on Tuesday urging him to end the annual Thanksgiving turkey pardon ceremony. The group says Trump should show the “chutzpah” that past presidents lacked and become the first sitting president to nix the tradition.
summary: People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals sent a Tuesday letter to President Trump urging him to end the annual turkey pardon ceremony. The group said Trump should show the “chutzpah” that previous presidents lacked.

title: Kelly: Democrats to discuss moving up Schumer-Van Hollen leadership vote
content: Sen. Mark Kelly (D-Ariz.), a supporter of Sen. Chuck Schumer’s (D-N. Y.) bid for majority leader, endorsed moving up the date of the Senate’s Democratic leadership election on Tuesday. Kelly stated that his party colleagues will discuss the proposal, adding that taking action now to move forward is likely a good idea.
summary: Kelly: Democrats to discuss moving up Schumer-Van Hollen leadership vote.

title: Hakeem Jeffries’s road to the Speakership will be nothing like Nancy Pelosi’s in 2018
content: Rep. Hakeem Jeffries is set to be re-elected as Democratic leader. This follows a period of successful fundraising and caucus unity during the second Trump administration.

content: Lawmakers from both parties urged Congress to pass a major bipartisan permitting reform bill before the legislative branch’s composition changes next year. Speaking at The Hill’s Bipartisan Blueprint event on Tuesday, members of Congress emphasized the urgency of acting now to advance the legislation.
summary: Lawmakers from both parties are urging Congress to pass a major bipartisan permitting reform bill before the legislative makeup changes next year. Members of Congress emphasized the urgency of acting now at The Hill’s Bipartisan Blueprint event.

content: Sen. Josh Hawley (R‑Mo.) has asked for an explanation of the FAA outage, dismissing the claim that a router in Arkansas caused it as “a little hard to believe.” He told reporters in the Senate that the full Senate should be briefed on what is happening, noting that “all of these outages” are a concern.

content: Elon Musk said on Monday that Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy declined a free Starlink offer for the FAA. Musk wrote that the offer was not needed, but he suggested it was.

content: After the midterms, a Democratic congressman declared that DEI is back. The question now is what Democrats’ ascendance will mean for diversity initiatives that the Trump administration has relentlessly attacked.

content: President Trump has arrived in Manila, marking the first stop of a three‑day Asia tour. The trip will later take him to China, where he is set to participate in historic three‑way nuclear talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.
summary: Trump arrives in Philippines to kick off Asia trip.

title: Google faces worst stock day as Planet Money questions its innovator's dilemma
content: In late October, Google experienced its worst stock day ever as a public company. The Planet Money newsletter questions whether the company is caught in “the innovator’s dilemma” as it navigates the AI race. The piece includes an image credit to Dave Rowland/Getty Images.
summary: In late October, Google experienced its worst stock day in its history as a public company. The Planet Money newsletter asks whether Google has been caught in the innovator's dilemma.

title: Sen. Jack Reed Calls for FAA Oversight Plan, Not Just Extra Funding
content: Sen. Jack Reed expressed concerns regarding the FAA’s oversight of contractors following last week’s nationwide ground stop. He criticized the Trump administration’s request for an additional $50 billion in funding, stating that the agency requires a real plan rather than just more money.
summary: Sen. Jack Reed raised concerns about FAA oversight of contractors after last week's nationwide ground stop. He criticized the Trump administration's request for $50 billion in additional funding.

title: Huang says he'd be honored to return to Nvidia as he agrees to testify to Congress
content: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has stated he would be "honored" to return to the company as he agrees to testify before Congress. These remarks emerge amid arguments from some in Silicon Valley suggesting Huang was pushed out of the company too quickly during a period of national security scandals.
summary: Former Nvidia CEO Huang said he would be honored to return to Nvidia. He agreed to testify before Congress, while some Silicon Valley observers argue he was pushed out too quickly amid national security scandals.
